_notes: Planet surfaces for the game prototype (game/): a hex grid on 3D terrain. The game starts in orbit: the scan shows terrain and rough deposit hints per region; the player picks a landing site, the colony pod descends, and survey rovers reveal exact deposits as they drive. terrain: move_cost = effort to enter a tile (unit speed is effort per second); height = visual relief level. planets: per planet class, how a surface is generated. Elevation and moisture come from deterministic noise (feature_size = tiles per noise cell) and are ranked, so thresholds are shares of the map: elevation ocean 0.30 = the lowest 30% of tiles are ocean, below shallows = shallows, from hills up = hills, from mountains up = mountains, the rest is lowland; within lowland, moisture picks the terrain; polar_rows at top and bottom become polar_terrain. deposits: rolled per tile on matching terrain (coastal = must touch water); amounts are ranges. hints: region totals below likely = traces, below rich = likely, otherwise rich. landing: where a colony pod may set down (tile terrain, and every neighbour must be passable land), how long it falls, what it brings (start_stock, the hub building, units) and how far the landing reveals. build_menu: buildings the player can place on the surface (their costs and stats are in buildings.json: build_seconds, output_per_min, upkeep_per_min, extract_per_min, requires_deposit; the hub's build_radius and build_queues limit where and how many build at once). Tiles must be surveyed and buildable to build on. Power: power_resource (energy) is not stockpiled on a surface; each base (a colony core and the buildings in its radius) has a power budget: power_supply of its working buildings vs power_use; when use exceeds supply, every power user at that base runs at supply/use speed. Levels: a core upgrades along upgrades_to (Colony Hub 1 → Colonial Administration 2 → Planetary Capital 3), paying the next level's cost and taking its build_seconds; it keeps working meanwhile. Storage: stockpiled materials (everything except storage_exempt) share one capacity per player, the sum of storage on their finished buildings (the hub's vault, Storage Containers, refineries); mining stops when it is full. Hills and plains hold raw ore, which an Ore Refinery turns into metal. salvage_refund: share of the cost returned when a finished building is salvaged. units: speed = move effort per second; mark = which mark of a vehicle line it is (1-3: survey_rover is the Mk I Scout, survey_rover_mk2 the Mk II Surveyor, survey_rover_mk3 the Mk III Explorer); cost and build_seconds = what a Vehicle Bay charges and takes to assemble one; a unit with extract_per_min is a mining crawler: it unfurls on a deposit (deploy_seconds), fills a hopper and sends each full load home as a cargo pod that flies pod_speed tiles per second to the nearest storage building or refinery. breakdown: while mining, each minute has chance_per_min of a breakdown; the severity is picked by weight and knocks damage (a range) off its integrity (100 = perfect); an explosion also loses the load in the hopper. A broken crawler folds up, can't mine, and drives slower (down to slowest_drive of its speed at 0 integrity). repair: drive it onto a colony core's tile (the repair pad beside the hub); after crew_seconds (the repair crew walking out) it regains per_second integrity, paying cost_per_point for each point, until it is back to 100. maintenance: buildings with wear_per_min lose that much condition (0..100) a minute while they work; below decline_below their output falls toward slowest_output at 0, and each minute they may break down outright (chance rising to break_chance_per_min_at_zero at 0); a broken building stops until maintained. Manual maintenance: the base's crew walks out (crew_walk_seconds + crew_seconds_per_tile per tile from the core), one job at a time per base, and restores repair_per_second, paying cost_per_point; buildings with auto_maintain (a top level, or the Automated Maintenance tech) fix themselves with drones whenever they drop below auto_below. research: surface techs a Research Lab works on (cost in research points; requires = techs needed first); modifiers add to building stats (speed, yield, wear) for the listed buildings (all buildings when none are listed), auto_maintain turns on drones, breakdown scales a unit's breakdown chance; ids shared with tech_tree.json are the same tech (deep_core_mining). orbit: the player's ship over the planet (name and ships.json class per faction), its cargo hold, and ways down: outpost_drop (a new Colony Hub at a safe site at least min_distance tiles from your other cores, after the first landing), shuttle (the drop ship: flies a payload unit down to a safe tile and goes back up), satellite (orbits over a band of band_rows rows and sweeps it every sweep_seconds, surveying it), transporter (levels by era, overridden per faction; range = tiles from your nearest base or unit, 0 = anywhere; cargo = supplies from the hold per beam; cooldown between beams). hud_resources: the stockpiled resources shown in the top bar, in order. unit_names: every new unit (landed, delivered or built) gets a name from pool and a number from the numbers range, in a random-looking order from the map seed; a player never gets the same name or number twice (when the pool runs out names go on as NAME II, NAME III...; when the numbers run out they go on with three digits). All numbers are placeholders.

research.name: Improved Smelting
research.effect: Refineries get 20% more metal from every load of ore.
research.description: Better furnace control and slag recovery pull more metal out of every load. Refineries get 20% more duranium and tritanium from the same ore, so each crawler load goes further.

research.name: Ore Conveyors
research.effect: Mines, deep-core mines and refineries work 20% faster.
research.description: Automated conveyor lines move ore from the drill heads into storage and from storage into the smelters, without crews hauling it by hand. Mines, deep-core mines and refineries all work 20% faster.

research.name: Preventive Maintenance
research.description: Inspection rounds and replacement schedules catch worn parts before they fail. Every building wears 30% slower, so breakdowns are rarer and the crew is needed less often.

research.name: Automated Maintenance
research.effect: Maintenance drones fix any building below 70% without a crew (parts still cost duranium).
research.description: Small maintenance drones patrol your bases and repair any building that drops below 70% condition, without waiting for the crew. Parts still cost duranium.

research.name: Alloy Metallurgy
research.effect: Alloy Foundries work 25% faster and get 10% more parasteel.
research.description: Refined alloy recipes and better crucibles for parasteel production. Alloy Foundries work 25% faster and get 10% more parasteel from each batch.

research.name: Reinforced Drills
research.effect: Mining crawlers break down half as often.
research.description: Tougher drill strings, shock mounts and better cooling for the mining crawler's rig. Crawlers break down half as often while mining.

research.name: Deep-Core Mining
research.effect: Unlocks the Deep-Core Mine: reopen a used-up deposit once at 50%.
research.description: Drilling techniques that reach past the depleted upper layers of a deposit. Unlocks the Deep-Core Mine, which reopens a used-up deposit once at half its original size.

units.description: Three officers with tricorders and a field kit, beamed or flown down from the ship. Slow on foot, but they survey the ground around them like a rover.

The Mk I Scout: a light four-wheeled rover with a sensor puck on a whip antenna. It reveals the exact deposits around wherever it drives, and it's the cheapest way to find ground worth mining. Two land with the colony.
The Mk II Surveyor: a six-wheeled rover with a spinning sensor dish. A little faster than the Scout, and it surveys a wider ring of ground around it, so it maps new land quicker.
The Mk III Explorer: a long six-wheeler on big tyres with a sensor turret. The fastest rover, and it surveys the widest area, for long trips far from your bases. It needs a little dilithium to build.

A tracked mining rig that drives to a deposit anywhere on the map, unfurls and mines it. Each full hopper flies home as a cargo pod to your nearest storage. It can break down while mining and is repaired on the Colony Hub's pad.
